text:
sam: Heads up — onboarding run found a weird parity issue: Node sampleapp + Ruby SDK + server retry path produced mismatched embedding dims and some entries became NaN in the rerank step.

rachael: NaN? That sounds nasty. Minimal repro?

sam: Sampleapp sends mixed vectors but we recently added an "optimized wire" for small batches that base64-encodes compact Float16 buffers into a batch header. When the SDK retry path serializes again it sometimes uses base64 vs raw JSON list depending on the code path. Ruby deserializer interpreted the base64 as a length-prefixed blob and truncated trailing floats, so dims dropped from 128 -> 120 for some items. Downstream cosine calc then produced NaN/dim mismatch.

diego: Do you have the logged outgoing and received shapes?

sam: Logged outgoing (simplified):
```
{"batch_meta":"compact:v1","items":[{"id":"u1","vec_base64":"..."},{"id":"u2","vec_base64":"..."}]}
```
On retry the Node helper re-serialized to the JSON-list path:```
{"items":[{"id":"u1","vec":[0.1,0.2,...]},{"id":"u2","vec":[0.5,0.6,...]}]}
```
Server normalizes and returns per-item embeddings by position. But Ruby SDK, hitting an alternate cached path, decoded the base64 into a byte buffer and re-sliced it incorrectly (off-by-8) when retries merged chunks -> u2 lost 8 floats.

rachael: So three problems colliding: (1) two wire formats (base64 compact vs JSON list), (2) retry/merge paths pick different serializers, (3) decoder bugs in a specific SDK implementation.

diego: Short-term mitigation: sampleapp and onboarding docs should warn: avoid mixing wire modes for the same batch; prefer JSON list during onboarding. Also validate vector length on receive and fail fast with clear error instead of continuing and producing NaN.

sam: Agreed. I added a quick client-side check in sampleapp: after response, assert each embedding length == expected_dim and throw a helpful error listing id + observed_dim. That caught the bug quickly.

rachael: Parity fix ideas: 1) canonicalize wire format server-side: accept both but always echo normalized JSON-list in response with per-item id, 2) SDKs must share a serializer test fixture so retry paths exercise both encode formats, 3) add unit test in Ruby SDK around base64 decode + merge offsets.

devex-bot: Ticket DE-11011 created: "embed wire-format parity + retry-merge base64 truncation" linked to #eng-runtime and #sdk-ruby.

sam: Also saw a duplicate-id edge: when retry dedupe ran we ended up with duplicate ids if the helper didn't mark retried chunks with a retry token. That made server dedupe aggressive and drop items. Workaround: bump sampleapp to include per-item monotonic `_attempt_id` and require server to echo it back.

diego: Good call. Add that to DE-11011: require server echo of per-item id + optional attempt token; SDKs to attach `_attempt` metadata during retry.

rachael: For onboarding checklist: add "avoid compact wire during early onboarding; validate dims on response; include stable ids and attempt tokens when retries enabled". I'll update the doc.

sam: I've pushed a tiny sampleapp patch showing validation snippet and switching to JSON-list mode while we patch SDKs.

devex-bot: DE-11011 created and assigned to eng-runtime + sdk-ruby. Integration test suggestion added: simulate mixed wire formats + token refresh + 502 + randomized chunk reorder.

diego: One more note: add telemetry when we see dim mismatch to catch production hits early (count per-customer).

sam: Agreed. We should surface a DX alert in Console if more than 0.1% of batches have dim validation errors.

rachael: Thanks team. Closing this thread for the onboarding run; follow DE-11011 for SDK/server fixes. :thumbsup:
